comments.body:
The fundamental fix should live in the shared target-only sampler, not in DFlash or in any individual RNG producer.

The sampler's contract should be:

- verification coins are uniformly distributed on the half-open interval `[0, 1)`;
- a CDF bucket is selected iff `coin < cumulative_mass`;
- a candidate with zero target mass is never accepted.

Concretely, the minimal fix for the reported default-threshold path is:

```diff
- if (coin <= prob_acc / threshold_acc || target_prob_single >= threshold_single) {
+ if (coin < prob_acc / threshold_acc || target_prob_single >= threshold_single) {
```

I would also make the zero-mass invariant explicit so it remains true when `threshold_single == 0`:

```cpp
const bool has_target_mass = target_prob_single > DType(0);
if (has_target_mass &&
    (coin < prob_acc / threshold_acc ||
     target_prob_single >= threshold_single)) {
  // accept token
}
```

The explicit guard preserves the existing threshold equality behavior for every positive-probability candidate; it only prevents an actually zero-probability candidate from being accepted. It also agrees with the documented meaning of `threshold_single` as a target-probability threshold.

I suggest covering the contract at the native-kernel level with these boundary cases:

1. `target_prob == 0`, `coin == 0` -> reject.
2. Sibling masses `[0.25, 0, 0.75]`, `coin == 0.25` -> skip the empty bucket and select the next positive bucket.
3. Positive first bucket with `coin == 0` -> accept.
4. Unit cumulative mass with the largest float32 coin below 1 -> accept.
5. `target_prob == 0`, `threshold_single == 0` -> reject.

The DFlash and EAGLE reproducers in the issue can then serve as caller-level regression tests. Moving or offsetting the random grid to `(0, 1]` would merely hide this boundary for one caller and would leave the shared kernel contract inconsistent.

title: [Bug] Target-only speculative sampler can accept a zero-probability draft at RNG boundary
